title: GDAS foundation SST carries the July 2022 to July 2023 growth of the R1 ocean cold mean offset
abstract: We tested whether a larger NCEP R1 cold ocean offset occurs in the upstream GDAS foundation sea surface temperature (SST). We read the separate foundation and skin fields from operational netCDF archives. On a common ocean mask at 60 S to 60 N, R1 minus daily OISST v2.1 fell by 0.1169 K from 1 July 2022 to 1 July 2023. GDAS foundation minus OISST fell by 0.1208 K. R1 minus foundation changed by only +0.0039 K. The tropical changes were -0.2444 and -0.2185 K. Thus the sampled mean cold-offset growth is present upstream, not solely in R1 processing. Two 2023 snapshots also give foundation means within 0.0311 K of R1, while skin is 0.1410 to 0.2140 K colder than foundation. This distinction matters for archive proxy tests. However, R1-foundation grid-point RMSE is 0.364 to 0.405 K. Regional residuals and timing checks prevent an exact field-match claim. Three selected dates do not establish annual means, the full change history or the physical cause. Exact source hashes, byte-range retrieval, an offline extraction check, code and aggregate results are included. Raw external grids stay outside the publication.

display.caption: Two July dates on one ocean mask. The mean cold-offset growth occurs in both R1 and GDAS foundation SST. These are snapshots, not annual means.
Foundation and skin temperature give different absolute comparisons on two 2023 dates.
Mean agreement leaves substantial grid-point differences between R1 and GDAS foundation SST.

citations.reason: Extends the cold boundary finding with a direct upstream foundation-field comparison.
Uses its documented switch notice and motivates replacement of the skin proxy by the separate foundation field. This is related evidence, not independent validation.
